mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 1% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5 percentage points over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises while CPIAUCSL falls by >0.5pp over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by more than 0.5pp over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening consumer demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both rise by >1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS rise by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which typically precedes aggressive monetary tightening and higher discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE remains below 4% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) below 900,000 units for six consecutive months signals a prolonged housing market downturn, which reduces construction-related economic activity and corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST remains below 900,000 for six consecutive months.
